title: Choices Speak Louder than Questions
claim: Instruction tuning and task instructions leave choice sensitivity largely unchanged, which stays high for cloze and varies strongly by input format.
layout: Single grouped bar chart, three model groups, hatched vs solid bars, legend below
description: A single grouped bar chart titled HellaSwag. The y-axis is Choice Sensitivity, from 0 to about 0.65. The x-axis has three instruct-tuned models: Llama 3.1-8B Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B Instruct and Mistral-7B Instruct-v0.3. Each model has twelve bars in color pairs. Blue is the cloze format, orange is symbols and green is probably hybrid. Within each pair, a light bar means without instruction and a dark bar means with instruction. Hatched bars appear to use a second scoring variant. Cloze bars are tallest, around 0.55 to 0.65. Symbol bars are lowest, down to about 0.1 for Mistral. A legend runs along the bottom and is cut off on the right. The eye goes first to the tall blue bars at the left of each group.
caption: The impact of instruction tuning and task instructions on choice sensitivity.
abstract: Recent findings raise concerns about whether the evaluation of Multiple-Choice Question Answering (MCQA) accurately reflects the comprehension abilities of large language models. This paper explores the concept of choice sensitivity, which refers to the tendency for model decisions to be more influenced by the answer options than by a genuine understanding of the question. We introduce a new scoring method called Normalized Probability Shift by the Question (NPSQ), designed to isolate the impact of the question itself and provide a more reliable assessment of comprehension. Through experiments involving various input formats, including cloze, symbols, and hybrid formats, we find that traditional scoring methods - such as those based on log-likelihood or its length-normalized variant - are vulnerable to superficial characteristics of the answer choices. In contrast, NPSQ remains stable even when modifications are made to the answer options.
